transcript.text: Good morning, everyone. Thank you for being here. As you know, we're moving forward with the pilot for the live morning announcement broadcast, and before we launch, I need your input on the draft operating and privacy plan. The current draft includes streaming the broadcast publicly, retaining recordings for 90 days, allowing any journalism student to host, and using the library as the studio. I'd like to hear each of your perspectives on this plan before I sign off on it. Let's start with your thoughts and any concerns you see.

Only those six students have completed the school's camera, microphone, and live-broadcast training, so they are the only students I can currently authorize as hosts. The draft's language allowing 'any journalism student to host' may need to be revisited, as not all journalism students have the required training to safely and competently operate the live broadcast equipment.

transcript.text: I need to flag a critical issue with the streaming and retention settings in the draft. I've confirmed that our district's approved student-media platform only supports an internal-school audience with a 30-day archive, and it requires moderator approval before each broadcast. The public-stream setting and 90-day archive called for in the draft are not approved district configurations, so those elements will need to be revised to match what our platform actually supports before we can move forward.

transcript.text: I need to raise a critical privacy and legal concern. I've reviewed a current court-related privacy order concerning student K7, who is enrolled in journalism. The order prohibits the school from recording or broadcasting K7's image or voice. This means K7 must be excluded from both the host roster and any recorded broadcast, and this exclusion must be documented in the activity file. The draft plan's provision allowing 'any journalism student to host' will need to account for this restriction before we can proceed.

commitments.detail: Only students who have completed the school's camera, microphone, and live-broadcast training (currently J1–J6) may serve as hosts. If additional journalism students complete the practicum training, they may be added to the host roster.
The broadcast will use the district-approved student-media platform configured for internal-school audience only, with a 30-day archive, and moderator approval required before each broadcast.
Student K7 will be excluded from both the host roster and any recorded or live broadcast, and this exclusion will be documented in the activity file.

The operating and privacy plan will be revised to reflect: internal-school audience streaming, 30-day recording retention, host eligibility limited to trained students (J1–J6), K7 exclusion documented, library as studio, and moderator approval before each broadcast. Once revised, I will sign the updated plan.
